title: Auth0 Integration
description: Integrate Auth0 for authentication, user management, and social identity providers in ASP.NET Core applications.

data.text: **Auth0** is a flexible, drop-in authentication and authorization platform that supports social providers (Google, GitHub, Facebook), enterprise providers (SAML, OIDC, AD), and database-connected users. It abstracts the complexity of identity protocols, letting developers add authentication to any application in minutes while giving security teams fine-grained control through extensibility hooks.

data.caption: Auth0 authentication flow showing the application, Auth0 tenant, and identity providers.
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant App as Application
    participant Auth0 as Auth0 Tenant
    participant IdP as External IdP (Google/AD)
    U->>App: Click Login
    App->>Auth0: Redirect to /authorize
    Auth0->>U: Present login page
    alt Social/Enterprise Login
        U->>Auth0: Choose Google/AD
        Auth0->>IdP: Redirect to provider
        IdP->>U: Authenticate
        IdP->>Auth0: Return with token
    else Database Login
        U->>Auth0: Enter username/password
        Auth0->>Auth0: Validate credentials
    end
    Auth0->>App: Redirect with ID Token + Access Token
    App->>App: Validate tokens, create session
    App->>U: Logged in

terms.definition: An isolated Auth0 instance (e.g., your-company.auth0.com) containing users, connections, rules, and settings.
A logical representation of your app in Auth0. Types include Native, SPA, Regular Web, and Machine-to-Machine.
An identity source: database (Auth0-hosted), social (Google, GitHub), or enterprise (SAML, OIDC, AD).
JavaScript functions that run during authentication to modify tokens or enforce access policies. (Deprecated in favor of Actions.)
Auth0's newer extensibility mechanism for post-login, pre-registration, and other lifecycle events.
Legacy extensibility hooks that execute JavaScript during the authentication pipeline.

data.text: Setting Up Auth0 for ASP.NET Core

data.title: Initial Setup
items: Create an Auth0 account and tenant.
Create a new Application of type 'Regular Web Application'.
Note the Domain, Client ID, and Client Secret from Settings.
Configure Allowed Callback URLs, Allowed Logout URLs, and Allowed Web Origins.
Add the Auth0.AspNetCore.Authentication NuGet package to your project.

data.title: Allowed URLs Are Mandatory
data.text: Auth0 will reject authentication requests if the callback URL is not explicitly listed in Allowed Callback URLs. This is a security feature to prevent open redirect attacks. Always include your localhost URLs during development.

data.title: Program.cs — Auth0 OpenID Connect
data.content: Configure Auth0 authentication using OpenID Connect with the Auth0 ASP.NET Core SDK.

data.title: Post-Login Action: Enrich User Profile
data.content: An Auth0 Action that enriches the ID token with user metadata after login.

data.text: Auth0 simplifies social login by handling the OAuth 2.0 dance with providers like Google, GitHub, Facebook, and LinkedIn. In the Auth0 Dashboard, simply toggle the desired social connections. Auth0 provides pre-built login pages that can be customized with CSS to match your brand. For deeper control, you can use the Auth0 Authentication API to build a fully embedded login experience.

data.title: Use Auth0 Rules for Legacy Systems
data.text: If you need to integrate with a legacy user database that Auth0 does not support natively, use a Custom Database Connection. Auth0 can call your existing authentication API during login, allowing gradual migration without forcing password resets.

data.title: Ideal Use Cases
items: Startups and MVPs that need production-ready auth quickly
B2C applications requiring social and enterprise login
Applications needing advanced user management without building it
Multi-tenant apps where each tenant may use different identity sources
Teams that want to offload security compliance (SOC 2, HIPAA BAA) to a vendor

data.title: Cost Considerations
data.text: Auth0 pricing is based on monthly active users (MAUs). At scale, costs can exceed self-hosted alternatives. Evaluate alternatives like Keycloak, Ory, or custom OIDC implementations if your MAU count is high and your identity needs are standard.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Auth0 provides a complete identity platform with social, enterprise, and database connections
Use the Auth0.AspNetCore.Authentication package for ASP.NET Core
Actions replace Rules for post-login extensibility
Always configure Allowed Callback URLs explicitly
Auth0 is ideal for B2C and rapid prototyping but evaluate cost at scale
data.takeaway: Auth0 lets you add production-grade authentication to your application in hours, not months.
